relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: one targets the CGRP receptor (erenumab), and the other three target the CGRP ligand

relationships.subject: erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: The findings of this study suggest that the receptor-mAb, erenumab, did not modify the sensory thresholds following treatment.

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: galcanezumab, an anti-CGRP-ligand mAb, exerts a trigeminal dermatome-specific pain modulatory effect, possibly by reversing existing hypersensitivity

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP not only binds to CGRP receptors, but also to the amylin-1 receptor, with a binding affinity similar to that of amylin

key_findings: Erenumab (70 mg and 140 mg) produced no change in QST thresholds in V1 or forearm in two migraine cohorts, unlike historical galcanezumab data showing trigeminal-specific threshold normalization.
Authors propose ligand vs receptor anti-CGRP mAbs act via different mechanisms (e.g., amylin-1 receptor), supporting class switching in non-responders.
